PAPERS.short: Ouimette PMS5003 PurpleAir internal heating hygroscopic mass reduction 2026
PAPERS.title: Air Flow, Heat Transfer, and Hygroscopic Aerosol Mass Reduction in the Plantower PMS5003 Sensor and PurpleAir Monitor
PAPERS.pm: PMS5003 / PurpleAir PM2.5 vs Teledyne T640x; detection-zone T and RH
PAPERS.geo: USA (Santa Rosa, California; Winston-Salem, North Carolina)
PAPERS.endpoint: Not applicable (sample RH and reported PM2.5 bias)
PAPERS.n: Lab and field work on temperature in the particle detection zone of the PMS5003, standalone and inside a PurpleAir. The PurpleAir housing warms the detection zone more than a bare PMS5003, lowering sample RH; a wraparound USB heater pushed sample RH down to regulatory-monitor conditions. In Santa Rosa and Winston-Salem (against a T640x), external heating lowered reported PM2.5 at high ambient RH, and the unheated PurpleAir already read below a standalone PMS. CFD characterised airflow, residence time and temperature. Limitation: two sites, no quantified bias reduction or growth-factor fit in the abstract; preprint. Relevance: high - EPA-style RH corrections assume ambient RH, but the sensor sees a warmed, drier sample; corrections built on bare-PMS data may not transfer to housed units.

PAPERS.short: Nahian Siegel in-situ testing in-duct air cleaners residential 2026
PAPERS.title: In-situ testing of in-duct air cleaners in residential buildings
PAPERS.pm: Residential in-duct air cleaner performance (particle removal presumed)
PAPERS.endpoint: Not applicable (in-situ device performance)
PAPERS.n: Title and authors only (Nahian, Siegel); no abstract retrievable at harvest from Crossref, Europe PMC or Semantic Scholar. The title describes in-situ testing of in-duct air cleaners (filters or electronic cleaners in forced-air systems) in occupied homes, presumably measuring particle removal under real operation. Country, number of homes, test protocol and removal metrics cannot be stated. Limitation: unverifiable beyond the title; in-situ effectiveness depends on HVAC runtime fraction, which lab single-pass efficiency ignores. Relevance: moderate - indoor LCS networks are the practical tool for verifying such devices in homes.

PAPERS.short: Li built environment sleep duration air pollution mediation Yinzhou cohort 2026
PAPERS.title: Association between built environment and sleep duration mediated by air pollution: a cohort study in China
PAPERS.pm: Residential PM10, PM2.5, NO2 (modelled annual) as mediators
PAPERS.endpoint: Change in self-reported sleep duration
PAPERS.n: Yinzhou cohort, 18,891 adults, baseline 2015-2017 and follow-up 2021-2023; quantile g-computation for a built-environment mixture and SEM for mediation. Per quartile of the mixture: +0.057 h/year sleep (0.039-0.075). Per IQR, PM10, PM2.5 and NO2 were associated with -0.027, -0.048 and -0.071 h sleep. PM2.5 mediated up to 21.5% of the green-space effect; NO2 up to 45.3% of the walkability effect. Limitation: self-reported sleep, and SEM mediation needs no unmeasured mediator-outcome confounding - noise and light at night co-vary with traffic pollution and are only partly modelled. Relevance: low-moderate - mediation of this kind needs better spatial exposure, not more covariates.

PAPERS.short: Poland air pollution COPD asthma emergency admissions DLNM heating season 2026
PAPERS.title: Air pollution and respiratory admissions in Poland: a nationwide DLNM analysis of COPD and asthma
PAPERS.pm: PM10, PM2.5, NO2, SO2, PAHs and metals in PM10 (national monitoring)
PAPERS.endpoint: Emergency hospitalisations for COPD and asthma
PAPERS.n: National registry: 625,597 COPD and 153,563 asthma emergency admissions (32,893 paediatric), DLNM lag 0-10, stratified by heating season. Associations appeared only in the heating season: COPD RR per IQR PM2.5 1.044, PM10 1.039, SO2 1.055; lead 1.072, benzo[a]anthracene 1.057. Adult asthma stronger (PM2.5 1.100). In children, PM was not significant; arsenic (1.124) and ozone (1.115) were. NO2 null throughout. No CIs in the abstract. Limitation: component and pollutant RRs come from single-pollutant models on collinear coal-combustion tracers, so 'lead' and 'PAH' effects cannot be separated from PM2.5; conference abstract. Relevance: moderate - heating-season coal signatures are where speciation-capable nodes add value over mass.

PAPERS.short: K-HEALTHinAIR indoor PM2.5 COPD attributable burden Spanish households 2026
PAPERS.title: Attributable Burden of COPD from Indoor PM2.5 Exposure in Spanish Households, 2025
PAPERS.pm: Measured indoor PM2.5 in Spanish homes (K-HEALTHinAIR)
PAPERS.endpoint: COPD DALYs attributable to indoor PM2.5
PAPERS.n: Comparative risk assessment combining measured household PM2.5 (K-HEALTHinAIR), GBD 2023 Spanish rates and published exposure-response functions. Mean attributable COPD burden ~116 thousand DALYs; by household type, homes with smokers 327 thousand, air-conditioning for heating 183 thousand, no climate control 192 thousand, gas cooking 119 thousand. Limitation: applying ambient-derived ERFs to indoor PM2.5 of different composition (tobacco, cooking) and scaling household-type estimates to national totals as if every home were that type; the subgroup figures are not additive and no uncertainty is given. Conference abstract. Relevance: moderate - burden estimates driven by low-cost indoor measurements.

PAPERS.short: Scotland prenatal PM2.5 infant amoxicillin birthweight mediation 2026
PAPERS.title: Prenatal PM2.5 and Infant Antibiotics: Birth-Weight Mediation via Causal Analysis
PAPERS.pm: Annual postcode PM2.5, pregnancy-month weighted (mean 7 ug/m3)
PAPERS.endpoint: >=1 amoxicillin prescription in first year (respiratory infection proxy)
PAPERS.n: All Scottish singleton births 2009-2018, n=498,123, linked registries; g-computation mediation comparing observed PM2.5 with a counterfactual of 5 ug/m3. Controlled direct effect OR 1.12 (1.10-1.14); interventional direct OR 1.12 (1.11-1.14); indirect via birthweight 0.99 (0.99-1.01). Limitation: exposure IQR is only 6-8 ug/m3, so a 12% excess over a ~2 ug/m3 counterfactual shift is implausibly large and points to residual area-level confounding (deprivation, prescribing culture); amoxicillin dispensing is a weak infection proxy. Preliminary conference abstract. Relevance: low-moderate - fine-scale exposure contrast is too narrow for postcode annual means.

PAPERS.short: UK Air Quality Cell PM10 plume back trajectory tyre fire Mexborough vulnerability 2026
PAPERS.title: Back trajectory modelled PM10 plumes: population vulnerability profile from an uncontrolled fire
PAPERS.pm: Incident PM10 monitoring + ADMS-STAR back-trajectory plume (22 hourly plumes)
PAPERS.endpoint: Population exposed by AQI band; socioeconomic profile
PAPERS.n: The UK Air Quality Cell monitored PM10 during an uncontrolled tyre fire; 22 hourly ADMS-STAR back-trajectory plumes were spatially averaged and overlaid on Output Areas. 24,952 residents fell in 'Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups' or worse; 7,856 (31.5%) in 'Hazardous' or beyond. Exposed areas had above-median deprivation, prior ill health and lower education. The modelling suggested field monitoring under-captured peaks. Limitation: AQI bands from a 24 h index were applied to hourly plume concentrations, and exposure is residential, ignoring sheltering and evacuation; no health outcomes. Conference abstract. Relevance: high - rapid-deploy sensor arrays around industrial fires would close the peak-capture gap the authors identify.

PAPERS.short: BEST-COST all-cause vs disease-specific exposure-response functions burden PM2.5 NO2 2026
PAPERS.title: Effect of all-cause versus disease-specific exposure-response functions on air pollution burden
PAPERS.pm: EEA PM2.5 and NO2 exposure; WHO-recommended ERFs
PAPERS.endpoint: Attributable years of life lost
PAPERS.n: BEST-COST burden estimates (healthiar R package) in five countries, comparing WHO all-cause mortality ERFs with disease-specific ERFs. Disease-specific YLL were 2-4x lower (ratio 0.26-0.52; median 0.42 for PM2.5, 0.31 for NO2). Country rankings were stable (Spearman rho >=0.90), but absolute agreement was moderate for PM2.5 (ICC 0.46) and poor for NO2 (0.15). Limitation: five countries is too few for inference (Wilcoxon p=0.0625); the gap partly reflects causes of death excluded from the disease-specific set, which is a substantive question, not a method artefact. Conference abstract. Relevance: moderate - ERF choice, not exposure error, dominates burden uncertainty.

PAPERS.short: Aloraini negative control PSCF CWT trajectory dust attribution Riyadh 2026
PAPERS.title: Transport Pathways Versus Dust Sources: A Negative-Control Test of Trajectory-Statistical Attribution in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia
PAPERS.pm: METAR present-weather dust codes (locally lifted vs suspension), 2016-2025
PAPERS.endpoint: Not applicable (validity of PSCF/CWT source attribution)
PAPERS.n: Ten years of Riyadh METARs separated locally lifted dust (BLDU/BLSA, 179 days) from suspended dust (DU/SA, 345). ERA5 models predicted local lifting better (held-out AUC 0.914 vs 0.765). PSCF and CWT fields from 14,612 HYSPLIT trajectories were then run on the local class as a negative control: it was more enriched over a priori source regions than the suspension class (permutation p <=0.007), and wind matching erased most structure in both. Dust days also fell 85.9% in 2023-2024 without model explanation. Limitation: METAR codes are visibility-based, not PM. Relevance: high - trajectory 'source maps' from single receptors, common in LCS papers, mostly reflect transport climatology.

PAPERS.short: Patras primary school classroom PM airborne viruses ventilation 2026
PAPERS.title: Dual burden of PM and airborne viruses in primary schools: A pilot study in Patras, Greece
PAPERS.pm: Classroom PM2.5/PM10 (triplicate) plus airborne virus RT-qPCR
PAPERS.endpoint: PM vs WHO AQG; detection of SARS-CoV-2, hMPV, RSV, rhinovirus, influenza A
PAPERS.n: March 2026 sampling in 28 classrooms of seven primary schools. Mean PM2.5 37.8 and PM10 109 ug/m3; every classroom exceeded the WHO 24 h guideline, and at least one respiratory virus was detected in every room (SARS-CoV-2 most often). Frequent natural ventilation was associated with lower PM (p <0.033, Cliff's delta >0.58) and less viral RNA. PM2.5/PM10 0.35 points to resuspension. Limitation: short occupied-hours sampling compared against a 24 h guideline overstates exceedance, and one month in one city; instrument type unstated. Conference abstract. Relevance: moderate - coarse-dominated classroom PM is where optical LCS under-read most.

PAPERS.short: K-HEALTHinAIR multicountry indoor air homes schools low-cost sensors 2026
PAPERS.title: Multicountry evaluation of indoor air in homes and schools: results from K-HEALTHinAIR project
PAPERS.pm: Low-cost sensor CO2, PM10, PM2.5 (annual 24 h means, 2025)
PAPERS.endpoint: Guideline exceedance frequency in homes and schools
PAPERS.n: Low-cost sensors in homes and schools across four countries, 2025. Home PM2.5 was elevated with smoking (93.9 ug/m3), air conditioning (34.8), gas cooking (29.5) and Dutch district heating (19.4). School PM2.5 was higher in Poland (22.0) than Austria (9.5). PM2.5 exceedance reached 56% of days in Austrian wood-heated homes and 36% in Spanish smokers' homes; CO2 exceedance was 41% in Austrian schools. Limitation: sensor calibration and RH correction are not described, so cross-country contrasts may partly be instrument and humidity artefacts; sampling of homes is unstated. Conference abstract. Relevance: high - a multi-country indoor LCS deployment whose QA is the open question.

PAPERS.short: ISVOLCAN Tajogaite volcano La Palma lung function obstructive pattern 2026
PAPERS.title: Lung function after Tajogaite volcano eruption in La Palma: ISVOLCAN study
PAPERS.pm: Residence area during the 2021 eruption; SO2 and PM exposure categories
PAPERS.endpoint: Obstructive spirometric pattern (FEV1/FVC <70%)
PAPERS.n: Random population sample of 604 adults (mean age 50; 62% women) with spirometry a median 424 days after the 85-day eruption. Obstruction prevalence 28.8%. Western (more exposed) residence: OR 1.64 (1.01-2.67); 1.74 (1.03-2.93) without prior respiratory disease. Intermediate SO2 exposure OR 1.98 (1.18-3.34). Limitation: a fixed FEV1/FVC <70% cut-off over-calls obstruction in older adults, no pre-eruption baseline exists, and residence area is a coarse proxy that cannot separate SO2 from volcanic PM; non-monotone SO2 categories. Conference abstract. Relevance: moderate - volcanic events are a case for rapidly deployed PM and SO2 sensor networks.

PAPERS.short: Yu Paris urban plume aerosol composition optical properties airborne ground 2026
PAPERS.title: Urban-to-downwind variations in aerosol composition and optical properties in the Paris urban plume from coordinated airborne and ground-based observations
PAPERS.pm: PM1 composition (AMS), particle number 80-200 nm, SSA, refractive index, AAE
PAPERS.endpoint: Not applicable (plume aerosol evolution over 2-6 h)
PAPERS.n: Coordinated ground and airborne measurements in Paris and its downwind plume, ~2-6 h transport. The plume modestly raised 80-200 nm particle number and moderately enhanced PM1; organics dominated PM1 throughout, with more oxidised organics downwind. Optical properties changed sharply: higher SSA at 450 and 630 nm downwind; refractive index moved from ~1.35-1.40 + 0.03-0.08i near source to ~1.45-1.50 + 0.015-0.02i downwind; AAE rose. Limitation: limited flights under specific meteorology; plume age is estimated, not tracked. Relevance: high - optical LCS use a single assumed refractive index; a 2-6 h change of this size shifts OPC mass conversion between urban and downwind nodes.

PAPERS.short: Upaul Khulna PM2.5 meteorology HYSPLIT random forest STL 2026
PAPERS.title: Meteorological and HYSPLIT-Derived Transport Influences on PM2.5 Exposure in a Khulna City, Bangladesh
PAPERS.pm: Hourly PM2.5 from the CAMS-8 station (2024); NASA POWER meteorology; HYSPLIT
PAPERS.endpoint: Not applicable (meteorological and transport drivers)
PAPERS.n: One year (2024) of hourly PM2.5 at a single Khulna station, analysed with MLR, Random Forest, STL and K-means on HYSPLIT trajectories. Winter mean ~121 ug/m3 vs ~15 in the monsoon. Temperature and pressure were top RF predictors (OOB R2 0.64); temperature and RH were negative in MLR. Winter air arrived on short north-westerly continental paths, monsoon air on long southerly maritime paths; STL residuals flagged pre-monsoon spikes (~138 ug/m3). Limitation: one station, one year, and reanalysis meteorology at ~50 km; season is collinear with every predictor, and the 'variance explained' shares are not additive. Preprint. Relevance: low-moderate - a coastal South Asian city with almost no monitoring, where LCS would add the spatial dimension.

PAPERS.short: Slovakia PM2.5 lung cancer mortality gender lag ecological 2026
PAPERS.title: PM2.5 exposure and lung cancer mortality in Slovakia: gender differences and delayed effects
PAPERS.pm: National population-weighted PM2.5 (Indicator of Population Exposure), 2010-2023
PAPERS.endpoint: Lung cancer mortality (GBD estimates)
PAPERS.n: National time-series ecology, 2010-2023: population-weighted PM2.5 fell from 24.4 to 15.2 ug/m3 while lung-cancer mortality fell from 30.7 to 25.3 per 100,000 (AAPC -1.5%), driven by men (56.8 to 42.6; AAPC -2.2%); female rates were flat (12.6). Correlation with PM2.5 r=0.95 overall and 0.97 in men, none in women; lags suggested emerging female associations. Limitation: 14 annual points of two monotonic trends correlate trivially; male smoking decline over the same period explains the male-only pattern, and the outcome is a GBD model output. Conference abstract. Relevance: low.

PAPERS.short: Dublin air pollution fungal spores respiratory admissions time series 2026
PAPERS.title: Short-term effects of air pollution and aeroallergens on respiratory admissions
PAPERS.pm: Daily NO2, PM2.5, PM1 (EPA Ireland); fungal spore counts
PAPERS.endpoint: Daily admissions for asthma, COPD and all respiratory causes
PAPERS.n: Dublin daily HIPE admissions with NO2, PM2.5, PM1, fungal spores and meteorology; negative-binomial time series, lags 0-7. NO2 was consistently associated with asthma, COPD and all respiratory admissions (~3-5% per unit, p <0.01); particulate effects were 'outcome-specific' and not quantified in the abstract; spores showed no independent short-term effect. Limitation: per-unit NO2 effects of 3-5% are implausibly large per ppb or ug/m3 and suggest an unstated scale; study years and PM results are missing; conference abstract. Relevance: low-moderate - Dublin's PM1 series is unusual, and spore counts pair naturally with optical sensor coarse channels.

PAPERS.short: Wilner public safety power shutoff wildfire PM2.5 healthcare California 2026
PAPERS.title: Co-exposure to planned power outages and wildfire PM2.5 and acute healthcare utilization in California: A time-stratified case-crossover study
PAPERS.pm: ZIP-level daily wildfire PM2.5 (per 10 ug/m3) jointly with public safety power shutoffs
PAPERS.endpoint: Respiratory, COPD, cardiovascular and psychiatric ED visits and unscheduled admissions
PAPERS.n: Statewide California encounters for adults 20+, time-stratified case-crossover, temperature-adjusted. Severe PSPS events alone: same-day respiratory encounters OR 1.06 (1.02-1.11), stronger for COPD. Joint PSPS and +10 ug/m3 wildfire PM2.5 vs neither: OR 1.16 (1.10-1.22), with multiplicative interaction. Cardiovascular and psychiatric encounters null. Limitation: PSPS is circuit-level but assigned by ZIP, and outage plausibly changes the exposure itself (no power for filtration or HVAC, more time outdoors or relocation), so the interaction mixes effect modification with exposure modification. Relevance: high - outages disable mains-powered sensors and purifiers precisely during smoke; battery-backed nodes are needed to measure this window.

PAPERS.short: Mercado-Velazquez low-cost sensors three-tier London calibration transferability 2026
PAPERS.title: How Accurate Are Low-Cost Air Quality Sensors? A 10-Month Study of Three-Tier Comparison with Three Calibration Methods and Cross-Site Transferability
PAPERS.pm: Low-cost optical PM2.5 plus MOS/electrochemical NO2, CO, O3 vs reference
PAPERS.geo: United Kingdom (London, two sites 1.6 km apart)
PAPERS.endpoint: Not applicable (sensor agreement, R2, seasonal drift, transfer)
PAPERS.n: Ten-month co-location of low-cost (MOS, optical), mid-cost electrochemical and reference instruments at two London sites. Calibration by manufacturer curve, T/RH linear regression and ML. Field-calibrated PM2.5 explained over half of reference variance at both sites, and linear calibration matched ML. PM2.5 calibrations trained April-October 2025 held through winter, whereas NO2 and CO did not; transferred between sites, PM2.5 reached R2 >=0.56 and gases R2 <=0.28. The mid-cost NO2 and low-cost O3 sensors failed under all methods. Limitation: two sites 1.6 km apart in one city share aerosol type and humidity regime, so 'transferability' is tested at its easiest. Relevance: high - supports simple T/RH regression for PM2.5 nodes and mandatory co-location for gas channels.

PAPERS.short: Ai optical trapping Raman single carbonaceous aerosol smoke 2026
PAPERS.title: In-Situ Single-Particle Sensing of Carbonaceous Aerosols in Freshly Generated Smoke Using Optical Trapping-Raman Spectroscopy
PAPERS.pm: Single airborne smoke particles (several um, ~10 pg), Raman spectra
PAPERS.endpoint: Not applicable (particle chemical fingerprinting)
PAPERS.n: Optical trapping-Raman spectroscopy captured smoke particles from nylon rope and plastic fibre ignited by the trapping laser itself, and analysed them airborne within seconds. Particles of several micrometres (~10 pg) gave full Raman fingerprints; band analysis separated two particle types, and spatially resolved spectra showed organic carbon and soot segregated within single particles. Limitation: freshly generated, supermicron, laser-ignited particles from two polymer fuels in an open chamber; ambient carbonaceous PM is mostly accumulation-mode, aged and far lighter, and the trapping laser may heat and alter what it measures. No throughput or detection-limit figures. Relevance: low-moderate - a reference technique for particle chemistry, not a field sensor.

PAPERS.short: Dhital on-road black carbon PM exposure Nepal route travel mode 2026
PAPERS.title: On-road exposure to black carbon and particulate matter in Nepal: Effects of route attributes and travel modes
PAPERS.pm: Equivalent BC (aethalometer), PM1, PM2.5, PM10 (portable optical)
PAPERS.endpoint: Not applicable (on-road exposure concentrations)
PAPERS.n: Mobile monitoring across Nepali road types, gradients and travel modes. Mean on-road eBC 45.7 +/- 32.5 ug/m3, ~11x background; eBC made up 51% of on-road PM2.5 and 75% of PM1. Concentrations rose from residential streets to intercity highways. Upgraded orbital-highway segments had lower PM2.5 and PM10 but unchanged eBC and PM1, so paving cut resuspended dust rather than exhaust. High-gradient (4.5%) segments: median eBC 86.7 vs 41.5 ug/m3 on 0.6% segments. Motorcycles gave the highest exposure, then non-AC and AC buses. Limitation: no n of runs or season control is reported, and the old-vs-upgraded comparison is not a before-after design. Relevance: high - shows optical PM2.5 nodes miss the exhaust-dominated BC contrast that drives on-road exposure.

PAPERS.short: Fan wildfire smoke indoor PM2.5 absenteeism Oklahoma Head Start OK-AIR 2026
PAPERS.title: Wildfire smoke, indoor and outdoor PM2.5, and sick-related absenteeism in Oklahoma Head Start early care and education centers
PAPERS.pm: Continuous classroom PM2.5 paired with hourly EPA outdoor PM2.5; HMS smoke days; FIRMS fire detections
PAPERS.endpoint: Indoor PM2.5 on smoke days; sick-related absence
PAPERS.n: Cohort 1 of the OK-AIR cluster-randomised 2x2 factorial trial (HEPA, upper-room UVGI): 5 centres, 20 classrooms, 204 children aged 0-5, 2023-2024. On smoke-impacted days, the intervention period (pooled arms) was associated with 29.0% lower indoor PM2.5 (22.8-34.7%) after adjustment for outdoor PM2.5. Each +100 in the 7-day mean of regional FIRMS fire detections: sick-related absence OR 1.106 (1.018-1.201). Limitation: the period contrast pools all arms, so it is not a HEPA effect, and smoke days cluster in Feb-Mar, confounded by respiratory-virus season; fire counts are a regional proxy, not exposure. Relevance: high - classroom sensor plus EPA outdoor pairing is a deployable I/O design for childcare networks.

PAPERS.short: Zhong air pollution years of life lost cancer Pudong Shanghai time series 2026
PAPERS.title: The short-term impact of ambient air pollution on years of life lost from cancer in Pudong New Area, Shanghai: A time series study
PAPERS.pm: Daily PM2.5, PM10, SO2, NO2, O3 (monitoring network)
PAPERS.endpoint: Cancer years of life lost and cancer mortality
PAPERS.n: Daily time series of cancer deaths and YLL in Pudong, 2013-2021, with DLNM (linear for YLL, quasi-Poisson for deaths). Per 10 ug/m3 at lag 0-1: PM2.5 +2.22 YLL (0.71-3.74), PM10 +1.04 (0.17-1.91); SO2, NO2 and O3 also positive. Effects were marginally larger in men, younger and more educated people. Limitation: short-term harvesting of cancer deaths is mostly mortality displacement in terminally ill patients, and single-pollutant models leave the PM2.5 estimate inseparable from co-pollutants; YLL per day is driven by a few young deaths, so the scale is unstable. Relevance: low - single-district monitor-average exposure.

PAPERS.short: Santoso air pollution noise greenness salivary cortisol BAMSE 2026
PAPERS.title: Air pollution, road traffic noise, and greenness in relation to salivary cortisol in young adults
PAPERS.pm: Address-level PM2.5, PM10, black carbon, NOx (dispersion models), prior year
PAPERS.endpoint: Morning and evening salivary cortisol at age 24
PAPERS.n: BAMSE birth cohort, n=1,148 at age 24; linear regression of salivary cortisol on prior-year modelled pollutants, noise and NDVI. No overall associations. In post hoc male subgroups, PM10 was associated with higher morning cortisol (beta 0.058, 0.003-0.112) as were NOx and noise, with greenness inverse; females showed opposite trends. Limitation: the only signals are exploratory sex-by-season subgroup contrasts after a null main analysis, with lower CIs at ~0; single-day cortisol is highly variable. Treat as null. Relevance: low - low-contrast Stockholm exposures modelled at the address.

PAPERS.short: Ruwali Lary US infant life expectancy environmental determinants machine learning 2026
PAPERS.title: Estimating Life Expectancy in the U.S.: Identifying Environmental Determinants and Disparities (2003 to 2019)
PAPERS.pm: 33 ECMWF reanalysis environmental variables incl. PM, sulphate and dust aerosol, O3, CO, HCHO
PAPERS.endpoint: Life expectancy, age <1 year (IHME)
PAPERS.n: County-level IHME life expectancy for the under-1 age group, contiguous US 2003-2019, regressed on 33 ECMWF environmental variables with ML. Marked north-south disparity, southern counties lowest. With only five variables the model reached R2 0.81 and RMSE 1.06 years on an independent test set. Beyond PM, O3 and CO, lower formaldehyde, sulphate and dust aerosol, more vegetation and lower wet-bulb temperature ranked as predictors of higher life expectancy. Limitation: no socioeconomic, race or healthcare covariates, so the south-north environmental gradient absorbs deprivation; feature importance is predictive, not causal, and IHME county estimates are themselves smoothed models. Relevance: moderate - a reanalysis-driven baseline that dense LCS data could sharpen.

PAPERS.short: Do PM2.5 superior cervical ganglion calcium channels satellite glia 2026
PAPERS.title: PM2.5 Exposure Disrupts Sympathetic Neurotransmission by Impairing Voltage-Gated Ca2+ Channels and Remodeling Satellite Glia in the Superior Cervical Ganglion
PAPERS.pm: Collected PM2.5, intracerebroventricular and ex vivo direct exposure
PAPERS.endpoint: SCG Ca2+ signalling, VGCC current density, norepinephrine release, glial markers
PAPERS.n: Rats received intracerebroventricular PM2.5; isolated superior cervical ganglia were also exposed directly. ICV PM2.5 raised hypothalamic TNF-alpha and IL-6. Direct exposure cut medium norepinephrine without changing tissue content; depolarisation-evoked Ca2+ responses fell after either route, and patch clamp showed lower VGCC current density without Cav alpha1 mRNA change. GFAP and Kir4.1 rose (satellite glia). Limitation: intracerebroventricular injection bypasses the lung and does not model inhalation dose or translocation; particle source and dose relevance are not given in the abstract. Relevance: low.

PAPERS.short: Ganse diesel exhaust particles cardiac metabolomics glycolytic shift rats 2026
PAPERS.title: Diesel Exhaust Particles Exposure Disrupts Cardiac Bioenergetics and Induces a Shift Towards Glycolytic Metabolism in Rats
PAPERS.pm: Diesel exhaust particles, intratracheal instillation 3x/week for 1 or 3 weeks
PAPERS.endpoint: Myocardial and plasma 1H-NMR metabolome
PAPERS.n: Sprague-Dawley rats instilled with DEP or saline three times weekly for one or three weeks. At one week, 17 of 22 myocardial metabolites changed: succinate, acetate, formate, 3-hydroxybutyrate, ATP and ADP fell; glucose and lactate rose, consistent with reduced oxidative metabolism and a glycolytic shift, plus nucleotide degradation. Most changes resolved by three weeks; plasma changes were modest. Limitation: intratracheal bolus dosing of a single reference DEP does not reproduce inhaled dose rate, group sizes are not stated, and transient changes that resolve under continued exposure question chronic relevance. Relevance: low.

PAPERS.short: Liu cerium dioxide scavenging environmentally persistent free radicals PM2.5 filtration review 2026
PAPERS.title: Cerium Dioxide-Based Scavenging of Environmentally Persistent Free Radicals in Fine Particulate Matter: A Prospective Review
PAPERS.pm: EPFRs on PM2.5 surfaces; CeO2-functionalised filter media (proposed)
PAPERS.endpoint: Not applicable (hypothesis: chemical quenching of EPFRs on captured PM2.5)
PAPERS.n: A hypothesis-stating review, explicitly not a validated result. EPFRs persist on PM2.5 for days to months and drive hydroxyl-radical generation by Fenton-like cycling after deposition. The authors propose migrating CeO2 Ce3+/Ce4+ redox cycling, an established antioxidant mechanism, into ambient-temperature air filters to quench EPFRs on captured particles, and argue that high-temperature catalytic uses of CeO2 are not a precedent. They list the open questions: direct quenching vs ROS interception, humidity, airflow, contact time, and CeO2 fate. Limitation: no data; the only cited support is gas-phase ROS scavenging in cigarette smoke. Relevance: low - filter chemistry, not measurement.

PAPERS.short: Alvi PMF trace elements PM10 Faisalabad health risk 2026
PAPERS.title: PMF Resolved Source Identification & Health Risk Assessment of Trace-elements in Airborne Particulate Matter (PM10) from South-Asian Megacity
PAPERS.pm: Filter PM10 with ICP-OES trace elements; PMF
PAPERS.endpoint: Source profiles; inhalation carcinogenic risk
PAPERS.n: Filter PM10 in Faisalabad analysed by ICP-OES: mean 517 +/- 206 ug/m3, ~10x WHO, higher in summer than autumn or winter. Element order Fe > Al > Si > Zn > Cu > Pb > Cd. PMF resolved seven sources: metal works, vehicle exhaust and non-exhaust, industrial fossil fuel, municipal waste incineration and industrial mixed dust. Cumulative carcinogenic risk 1.22e-3 (adults) and 5.05e-4 (children). Limitation: ICP-OES detection limits for As, Cr and Cd are marginal at these loadings, PMF with ~20 elements and no carbon or ions cannot separate combustion sources robustly, and n of samples is not given. Relevance: low-moderate - coarse, crustal-dominated PM10 at these levels saturates optical LCS assumptions.

PAPERS.short: Wang PM2.5-bound PAH association rules machine learning forecasting Nagoya 2026
PAPERS.title: Characterizing statistical association patterns and local forecasting of PM2.5-bound polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon concentrations in Nagoya, Japan
PAPERS.pm: Hourly PM2.5-bound PAHs, BC, NOx, oxidants, meteorology
PAPERS.endpoint: Not applicable (hourly PAH prediction; incremental lifetime cancer risk)
PAPERS.n: Hourly PM2.5-bound PAHs in Nagoya with association-rule mining and ML under time-blocked cross-validation. Low wind speed was the most consistent condition for PAH accumulation; BC and NOx peaked at rush hours. XGBoost and RF predicted high-molecular-weight PAHs best (R2 0.81-0.93, RMSE 0.02-0.11); SVR and MLP were poor. BaP dominated toxicity; lifetime cancer risks were below the USEPA negligible threshold. Limitation: a 10-day observation period, so the models learn one synoptic episode, and the authors themselves restrict the rules to site-specific description. Relevance: moderate - a BC-plus-meteorology proxy for PAHs is the kind of virtual sensor a network could run, if trained on far longer records.

PAPERS.short: Lovric ragweed sensitisation PM10 pollen model comparison Croatia ATOPICA 2026
PAPERS.title: Outdoor Environmental Risk Factors for Paediatric Ragweed Sensitisation: A Formal Model Comparison
PAPERS.pm: Area-level PM10 and NO2; regional ragweed pollen; CORINE land cover (5 km)
PAPERS.endpoint: Ragweed skin-prick sensitisation (wheal >=2 mm)
PAPERS.n: Re-analysis of 3,520 Croatian children from ATOPICA within EDIAQI; logistic models compared by AIC, adjusted for age and parental atopy. Sensitisation prevalence 10.8%. PM10 and categorical pollen area fit equally well (delta AIC 1.7) because both encode the same inland-coastal contrast; NO2 added nothing. Transitional woodland-shrub aOR 0.93 (0.90-0.97) survived Bonferroni; rural residence aOR 0.69 (0.50-0.96). Limitation: the authors state it directly - area-level exposure cannot separate particulate pollution from pollen, so a PM contribution can be neither confirmed nor excluded. Relevance: moderate - an explicit case where only sub-regional, co-located PM and pollen measurement could break the collinearity.
